headline: Berlin Supermarket Grows Fresh Lettuce on Its Own Roof
meta_description: A REWE supermarket in Berlin grows lettuce on its rooftop using hydroponic technology, cutting transportation time from miles to stairs. The farm could reshape…
summary_short: At a Berlin REWE supermarket, lettuce grown on the rooftop reaches shelves in hours, not days. The hydroponic farm uses waste heat and rainwater—and the model could expa…
body:
At the REWE supermarket in Berlin's Lankwitz district, the journey from farm to shelf takes minutes. Lettuce is cut and packaged by hand on the rooftop greenhouse, then carried downstairs before most shoppers arrive. The distance traveled is measured not in miles but in flights of stairs—a radical shortening of the supply chain that eliminates the truck, the distribution center, and the weeks of travel that lettuce normally endures. The store was built with this farm integrated into its design, with skylights throughout the grocery floor offering shoppers a view of what grows directly above them.

The rooftop operation runs on hydroponic technology year-round, meaning plants grow in just over three weeks with minimal soil. The system closes loops within the building itself: waste heat from refrigeration warms the greenhouse; rainwater collected on the roof waters the plants; solar power supplements the electricity. Nothing the building produces is wasted. Project lead Leschke notes that the farm eliminates the need for extra trucks to transport goods from producer to distribution center—a simple but profound redesign of logistics.

The greens grown here don't just serve the Lankwitz store. They're distributed to other REWE locations across Berlin and the surrounding region, demonstrating that rooftop farms can scale beyond single buildings. Research by Prajal Pradhan at the University of Groningen suggests urban agriculture could meet approximately 28 percent of Europe's total vegetable demand. Yet experts stress that such commercial projects should complement, not replace, community gardens—spaces where neighborhoods grow food together and share agricultural knowledge. For now, REWE offers public tours of the facility, while Leschke plans to build at least 20 supermarket rooftop farms across REWE regions within the next decade, reducing dependence on global supply chains.
quick_facts: REWE Lankwitz store grows lettuce on rooftop using hydroponic technology
Harvest-to-shelf journey measured in flights of stairs, not miles
Greenhouse heated by waste heat from store refrigeration equipment
Urban rooftop farms could supply 28% of Europe's vegetable needs
REWE plans at least 20 rooftop farms within ten years
